Most of these hypotheses rest on how training stability and convergence speed depend on the learning rate. The probe evidence supports this: at learning_rate_init=0.278, edits that lowered the learning rate or the depth recovered +35 to +59 points on segment and vehicle (experiments 56 and 64). The alpha interactions draw on general knowledge that strong L2 penalties cause underfitting, not on these probes. The 100 experiments did not test any configuration with alpha above 0.129.

| 3 | learning rate up | learning rate high | lower | Raising an already near-divergent rate pushes the net further into collapse. |
| 4 | learning rate down | learning rate low | lower | Lowering an already tiny rate deepens undertraining. |
| 5 | depth down | learning rate high | higher | Shallower nets are much more stable at high rates (exp. 56: up to +59 points). |
| 6 | depth up | learning rate high | lower | Extra layers amplify instability at high rates (exp. 54: −24.7 on segment). |
| 7 | alpha up | alpha high | lower | At alpha ≈ 0.13–1 more penalty causes underfitting, unlike the near-zero effect at small alpha. |
| 8 | alpha down | alpha high | higher | Relaxing a heavy penalty relieves underfitting, while at tiny alpha it does nothing. |
| 9 | batch size up | learning rate low | lower | With a tiny rate, fewer updates per epoch worsen undertraining. |
| 10 | batch size down | learning rate low | higher | More updates per epoch help a slowly learning net converge. |
